A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same TMCL study, with complete main text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–H. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support reliable matching throughout.

before.justification: v2 reports original continual-learning experiments on CIFAR-100 and ImageNet-100, downstream transfer results, robustness tests and ablations, including supplementary results in Appendix F.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental outcomes in Tables 1–6 and A2 and the accompanying figures and analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix C retain the same modulation-learning and consolidation procedures, objectives, components and pseudocode. Neither backbone implementation changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same CIFAR-100 and ImageNet-100 continual-learning tasks, nine downstream transfer datasets and noisy-label scenarios. Appendix F retains the ten-session CIFAR-100 experiment.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same CE, SupCon, VI, CaSSLe/PNR and CLS-ER methods and combinations. The additional literature baselines in Table 6 are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A preserve the same splits, label fractions, training budgets, model configurations, preprocessing and linear/kNN evaluation procedures. The ten-session protocol in Appendix F is unchanged.

E4.justification: The label-noise tests, modulation-strength sensitivity, transfer analyses, orthogonalization ablations, architectural ablations and CDNV analysis are identical in Tables 3–5, Figures 3–4 and Appendix B.

E5.justification: Seed counts and uncertainty reporting remain unchanged. Table 1 still specifies three seeds for ImageNet-100 and four for CIFAR-100 with standard deviations; Figure 4 retains minimum–maximum shading over four seeds.

E6.justification: All result entries and plotted findings are retained. For example, Table 1 reports identical VI+MI accuracies with 1% labels: 60.7±0.3 on CIFAR-100 and 62.0±0.2 on ImageNet-100. Appendix results also match.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(11), the orthogonality reasoning in Appendix D, and the transfer and CDNV definitions in Appendices B and E are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and discussion retain the same TMCL contribution, sparse-supervision and transfer-performance claims, and proposed biological role of modulations in balancing stability and plasticity.

C2.justification: The result interpretations and applicability qualifications remain identical, including explanations of label-noise robustness and architectural differences. Section 5 retains the limitations concerning incremental-task coverage, class-dependent memory growth and fully labeled performance.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains the same implementation details, hyperparameters, code link, A100 hardware, memory requirements and runtime information. Revised computing acknowledgements concern funding attribution and citations, without changing technical specifications or access instructions.

R1.justification: v3 adds the 2021 JURECA and JUWELS facility reports as references 104–105. The previously cited facility papers remain in supplementary references 115–116. Section 2 and the scientific positioning are unchanged.

P1.justification: The acknowledgements expand the JUWELS funding credit to name the Gauss Centre and NIC, removing the earlier neuroml grant identifier. The version/date stamp and citation numbering change; scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The acknowledgement and reference edits cause small spacing and reflow changes on pages 10–11 and 19, including slight positioning changes around Table 6. Figure designs, table structures, captions and appendix displays are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 revises computing attribution and facility citations while retaining the same scientific account, experimental evidence, reproducibility information and limitations, including the appendices. These administrative edits and small layout shifts produce no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
